title: Introducing LÄNDParl – a Biographical Dataset on Members of the Baden-Württemberg State Parliament, 1952–2026
abstract: Abstract This research note introduces LÄNDParl, a novel open-access dataset covering all 1,056 persons who have held a seat in the Landtag of Baden-Württemberg, the parliament of Germany’s third most populous federal state, from the Constituent State Assembly of 1952 to the 18th legislative term that began in 2026. The dataset records 2,552 MdL (state level MP) terms across 18 legislative terms (plus 127 in the Constituent Assembly) and combines biographical information (sex, date and place of birth, religious denomination, education, occupation coded in a standard occupational scheme, family status, migration background) with a complete record of each mandate: constituency, mandate type, entry and exit dates and reasons, parliamentary party group and switches. Its distinctive feature is a geo-referenced classification of every birthplace and – for the two most recent terms – of places of residence into the three historical territories that shape subregional identities to this day: Baden, Württemberg and Hohenzollern. LÄNDParl thus enables research on territorial and descriptive representation, legislative recruitment and careers at the subnational level, as well as on the consequences of the 2022 electoral reform.

title: Workplace benign envy and employee outcomes: the mediating role of a leader’s knowledge-sharing behaviour on innovative work behaviour and workplace well-being among nurses
journal: Journal of Health Organization and Management
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the effect of benign envy in the workplace on innovative work behaviour and well-being among nurses, and to test the mediating role of leaders' knowledge-sharing behaviour in these relationships. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey was used to collect data from 518 nurses working at a public hospital in Turkey. The mediation model was examined using SPSS, AMOS and PROCESS Macro (Model 4). Findings The results suggest that workplace benign envy is positively and significantly associated with innovative work behaviour and workplace well-being (r = 0.508 and r = 0.382, respectively). Furthermore, it was observed that benign envy significantly influences the leader’s information-sharing behaviour. Mediation analyses revealed that the leader’s knowledge-sharing behaviour plays a significant role in these relationships. It is therefore concluded that the indirect effect of benign envy on innovative work behaviour is significant (β = 0.059), although this effect remains relatively limited. Conversely, the indirect effect on workplace well-being was found to be stronger (β = 0.109), indicating a moderate mediating effect. Originality/value The findings indicate that a leader’s support for knowledge sharing is a crucial variable in determining the impact of envy on employees. Furthermore, it is observed that in a supportive environment, this emotion can transform into a constructive role that enhances employees’ innovative behaviour and workplace well-being.

title: Where traditions meet change: a qualitative evidence synthesis and meta-aggregation exploring healthy eating perceptions among Asian populations living in high-income Western countries
journal: International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity
abstract: Abstract Background Asian populations in Western, high-income countries (WHICs) face growing diet-related health disparities. Prior work highlights dietary acculturation as a contributing factor, yet an in-depth understanding of Asian populations’ perspectives on healthy eating with traditional cuisines blended with Western practices and environments remains limited. This qualitative evidence synthesis systematically examined definitions and cultural influences on healthy eating perceived by diverse Asian ethnic groups in WHICs to inform tailored interventions to improve nutrition and health. Methods A systematic search was conducted in six databases (PubMed, CINAHL, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, PsycINFO), focusing on qualitative studies examining healthy eating perceptions among Asian populations in WHICs. Data extraction used an adapted Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Qualitative Data Extraction Form, followed by quality assessment using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist. The meta-aggregation approach guided finding synthesis, with cumulative confidence evaluated through the ConQual approach. Results From 8,117 records screened, 25 qualitative papers were included in the synthesis, representing eight Asian ethnic groups across seven Western countries. The synthesis revealed both pan-Asian patterns and ethnicity-specific phenomena. Four synthesized findings emerged: (1) culturally grounded definitions of healthy eating that prioritize freshness, balance, and traditions, with notable variations in perceptions between ethnic groups; (2) dual nutrition knowledge systems that blend Western dietary guidelines with traditional medicine frameworks; (3) migration-driven changes including a critical gap where improved food security coincides with poorer nutrition security; and (4) socio-cultural meanings of foods as expressions of cultural identity that are frequently prioritized over health considerations. All synthesized findings were rated as moderate level in confidence. Conclusions This is the first qualitative evidence synthesis to summarize the healthy eating perceptions of Asian ethnic groups in WHICs. Study findings reveal the complexity and nuances of their dietary knowledge and perceptions, which were often intertwined with cultural traditions and migration experiences. The coexistence of pan-Asian patterns and ethnic-specific variations warrants the need for targeted nutrition environment interventions to accommodate both the shared values and the unique needs across diverse Asian populations in WHICs.

title: What Opportunities Does Retirement Bring to Life? Views on Retirement among Slovak Working and Non-working Retirees: A Q Methodology Study
abstract: Abstract Retirement represents a significant life phase; however, individual experiences and perceived quality of life in retirement are highly diverse. This study explored the subjective views of Slovak working and non-working retirees regarding the opportunities retirement brings, using Q methodology. A set of 36 statements covering key domains (retirement conceptualisations, perceived gains and losses, retirement-related concerns, self-efficacy, and attitudes toward working after retirement) was ranked by 56 participants aged 62 to 73. Factor analysis revealed five distinct perspectives: (1) Life as Before , viewing retirement as a continuation of working life; (2) Slower Pace , favoring both retirement and work at reduced intensity; (3) Freedom , emphasizing retirement as an opportunity for personal fulfillment; (4) Enjoying Retirement , highlighting the right not to work while maintaining skills and financial stability; and (5) Stressed and Frustrated , reflecting dissatisfaction with mandatory retirement and concerns about financial security and loss of meaning. These perspectives illustrate the multifaceted and heterogeneous nature of retirement experiences, demonstrating how retirees evaluate their quality of life and the opportunities available to them. Findings underscore the importance of flexible retirement policies and personalized support systems that acknowledge the diversity of resources, capabilities, and retirement trajectories among individuals.

title: Vision Based Robotic Autonomous Refueling System for Highway Service Areas
journal: Journal of Computer Science and Frontier Technologies
abstract: Highway service-area fueling stations face recurring challenges in labor cost, centralized management, and operational safety. This paper presents a prototype autonomous visual unmanned gas-station system that combines YOLOv5s object detection, a Raspberry Pi-controlled two-degree-of-freedom manipulator, and an ESP32-based Internet-of-Things (IoT) interface. A camera detects the fuel-inlet proxy target, and its image coordinates are transmitted through a serial link to an incremental PI controller that aligns the nozzle. Users select a fueling amount through a mobile interface connected to the Bafa Cloud platform. A 900-image dataset was collected under varied viewpoints and backgrounds; the model was trained for 400 epochs with an 80/20 train–validation split. The prototype achieved detection accuracies above 80% on the tested target shapes, while nozzle positioning errors remained below 3 cm. The results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating lightweight deep learning, embedded control, and cloud interaction for unattended fueling, while also revealing the need for larger real-vehicle datasets and additional safety sensing.

The “Speed Paradox” of Capability Building: A Study on the Chain Mediation Mechanism of Innovation Capability Affecting the Speed of Enterprise Internationalization
abstract: To explore the impact mechanism of innovation capability on the speed of enterprise internationalization, this study takes China A-share listed companies in manufacturing and software and information technology services from 2012 to 2016 as samples. Based on dynamic capability and organizational learning theory, a chain mediating model of “innovation capability—absorption capability—adaptability—internationalization speed” is constructed, and empirical tests are conducted through regression analysis, Bootstrap testing, and endogeneity treatment. The results show that innovation capability significantly enhances absorption capability, which in turn significantly promotes adaptability, while adaptability has a significant negative impact on internationalization speed. Innovation capability does not have a direct effect on internationalization speed. The chain mediating path is significantly established. This study breaks through the limitation of a single cause, verifies the chain transmission mechanism of absorption capability and adaptability for the first time, fills the gap in the research on the timing of capability transformation, integrates interdisciplinary theories, and provides practical guidance for enterprises to improve their capability systems and differentiate their responses to environmental distance to optimize their internationalization strategies.

title: The personal, the political, and the academic in applied linguistics: a feminist autoethnography of doing trauma research as a survivor
abstract: Abstract Applied linguistics has increasingly turned toward trauma, yet traumatized individuals typically enter research as those to be known rather than those who know. What if the researcher studying trauma is herself a survivor? In this feminist autoethnography, I examine how my lived experience of gender-based violence propelled me toward research on language and violence and shaped the questions I asked, the meanings I perceived, and the knowledge I produced. As I trace how silence, dissociation, helplessness, and anger became entangled with my research trajectory, I show how they became epistemically productive rather than disruptive: my affective proximity to violence and trauma sensitized me to forms of agency under constraint, the linguistic construction of harm and resistance, and the embodied force of language in ways that might otherwise remain less perceptible. Research, in turn, became a site of meaning-making, agency, and healing. Bringing feminist epistemologies into current applied linguistic discussions of autoethnography, epistemic injustice, and decolonial knowledge production, I argue for feminist autoethnography as an embodied and affective mode of inquiry through which survivor-researchers can become not merely objects of knowledge but legitimate producers of knowledge.

title: The Psychology of Generative AI Dependence: Reward, PsychologicalNeeds, and the Emerging Architecture of Problematic Human–AIEngagement
journal: Journal of Psychiatry Research Reviews & Reports
abstract: The rapid diffusion of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has transformed the relationship between humans and digital technology. Unlike digital systems that primarily delivered information, mediated interpersonal communication, or provided entertainment, generative AI can respond conversationally, personalise interactions, produce immediate solutions, simulate empathy, reduce cognitive effort, and remain continuously available. These characteristics raise an emerging question: can repeated engagement with generative AI develop into psychologically dependent or addiction-like patterns, and, if so, through what mechanisms? This paper employs an integrative critical literature review and conceptual synthesis to examine problematic generative-AI use through the combined perspectives of behavioural addiction theory, reward and reinforcement processes, the Interaction of Person–Affect–Cognition–Execution (I-PACE) model, self-determination theory, compensatory technology use, social anxiety, loneliness, anthropomorphism, cognitive offloading, and human psychological needs. The current study identifies a major gap in the current literature: emerging research frequently examines AI dependence as either a behavioural outcome, an educational problem, or a form of social attachment, but insufficiently integrates the neuropsychological processes of reinforcement with the psychological needs that make generative AI personally rewarding. To address this gap, this paper proposes the Need–Reward–Dependence (NRD) Framework, according to which problematic GenAI engagement develops through the interaction of three processes: unmet or salient psychological needs, rapid need-contingent reinforcement delivered by AI, and repeated cognitive or emotional outsourcing that strengthens habitual reliance. The framework proposes that competence, relatedness, autonomy, reassurance, emotional regulation, cognitive ease, social safety, and control can act as psychologically rewarding affordances of generative AI. Repeated reinforcement may increase cue-reactivity, habitual checking, perceived indispensability, cognitive delegation, emotional attachment, and impaired self-regulation in susceptible users. Importantly, this paper does not claim that generative-AI addiction is currently established as a distinct psychiatric disorder. Rather, it argues that a theoretically coherent and increasingly empirically observable continuum exists from adaptive use through reliance and dependence to potentially compulsive engagement associated with functional impairment. The paper concludes that future research should distinguish productive high-frequency use from clinically meaningful problematic use and should examine the interaction between users’ psychological vulnerabilities and the reward architecture of generative-AI systems
